title: The plan's week number and easy weeks keep counting the weeks a member was away
what: A followed plan's week is counted from its start day by the calendar only. A member who stops for 8 weeks comes back to 'Week 20 · easy week in week 24', and the easy week or the hardest 'leave 1 rep in the tank' week can land on the first week back. A plan with no start day takes its first workout ever as the start, so an old imported plan can read 'Week 150'. At the same time each exercise's target already says '8 weeks off, so a lighter start', so two parts of the same screen tell the member different stories.
expected: After a long break (the 6 weeks the targets already use) the plan restarts its week count, or at least does not put an easy week or the hardest week on the first week back, and the week line agrees with the lighter-start note.
who: members who follow a plan and take a break
how_often: every return after a long break
fix_line: Restart or pause the plan's week count after a break of 6 weeks or more

title: After a long break the finish screen calls a planned lighter workout just 'lighter' and may blame sleep
what: When a member returns after 6 weeks or more, the app itself sets lighter weights. On finishing, the big card compares with the workout from before the break and says 'Lighter than previous', and the line under it can say last night's sleep was short or give a protein tip, as if those were the reason. The real reason, the break the app planned for, is never named there. Easy weeks already get their own 'lighter on purpose' words; a break does not.
expected: The finish screen says the lighter total is the planned restart after N weeks off, and the sleep or protein line is not shown as the reason.
how_often: first workout after 6 weeks or more off
fix_line: Pass the break to the finish card and say 'lighter start after N weeks off'

items.reason: Gym tab badge = bell unread + talk unread + ask unread, the same stores the Gym tab shows (Crispy Curves SQL: 3 gym messages, 0 talk threads, 0 talk messages, 0 mate workouts, so a recount proves nothing). Workouts count, chart and feed all count every saved workout alike. Weekly goal is counted as days in Up next and the widget but as workouts in Progress: already a finding. Workout numbers live on the phone, not in the gym data.
Chart weeks and months, streak and rest days handle a first workout today and empty weeks (a gap draws as zero points); the plan week does not handle a gap of weeks.

Chart total is the sum of its own points; the recap's total and set count come from the same sets it lists; a drop shows 'Lighter than previous' with the exercise that moved most, but a planned drop after a long break is not named.

Chart point number (session totals by day) and 'See these workouts' list (same day field) are two functions with the same filter; length is end minus start everywhere, with pauses folded into the saved end.
On a long-gap case the exercise target (break-aware) disagrees with the plan week and the finish card (both not break-aware).
